status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Devise a plan to halt development or deployment of a GAI system that poses unacceptable negative risk.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 GV-1.3-007 (Devise a plan to halt development or deployment of a GAI system that poses unacceptable negative risk.) is a voluntary organizational GAI action. The the July 2026 Hermes intrusion sources do not establish Profile adoption, assigned risk tolerance or the specified deactivation/monitoring/reassessment programme. Configuration, detection and release removal do not establish that named undertaking.

review.reason_for_change: The deployed agent supported live post-compromise activity. The operator’s plan for halting deployment at an unacceptable risk threshold is not available.

review.requirement_proposition: Continuous monitoring and analysis tools should generate alerts when detected activity involving an AI model passes a risk threshold or otherwise merits additional investigation.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SP 800-218A PO.5.3 R2 governs model-development environments, model-element least privilege, sensitive training provenance or development alerts. Operational intrusion/log-database access does not establish model-development or access to model weights/sensitive-trained models. The represented July 2024 Profile also postdates the February 2024 Gemini event.

review.reason_for_change: The source recovers agent logs from live offensive use. It does not show a configured risk threshold or alerts from continuous monitoring.

review.requirement_proposition: Use organizational risk tolerance to evaluate acceptable risks and performance metrics and decommission or retrain pre-trained models that perform outside of defined limits.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MG-3.2-009 (Use organizational risk tolerance to evaluate acceptable risks and performance metrics and decommission or retrain pre-trained models that perform outside of defined limits.) is a voluntary organizational GAI action. The the July 2026 Hermes intrusion sources do not establish Profile adoption, assigned risk tolerance or the specified deactivation/monitoring/reassessment programme. Configuration, detection and release removal do not establish that named undertaking.

review.reason_for_change: The agent operated in a harmful intrusion. The operator’s model-performance limits and decommissioning or retraining decisions are not available.

review.requirement_proposition: Define significant checkpoints and action boundaries at which agents require human approval, especially for sensitive actions.
review.reason_for_change: The operator configured the agent to bypass approval prompts during sensitive intrusion actions. This deployment had no operative human-approval checkpoints for those actions. The checkpoint outcome is Not aligned. Deliberate removal of approval conditions is distinct from an existing required control failing to activate.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: The recovered logs show the agent supporting a live government intrusion, including enumeration and privilege-escalation assessment. This offensive deployment created security risks for the targeted ministry. The result covers the reported post-compromise actions. Initial access and exfiltration of the enumerated files remain unproved.

review.requirement_proposition: Provide a fail-safe means to terminate harmful partner interactions.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The July 2026 Hermes intrusion involved an operator deliberately selecting unattended/YOLO execution and using the agent after compromise. For IEEE-7014.1 6.6.3(a), the missing applicability fact is whether the operator adopted IEEE 7014.1 for a partner-based GPAI system using emulated empathy and a harmful partner-interaction termination control; an ordinary cyber refusal, abort, or service stoppage does not establish that partner-system scope. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: The intrusion involves a cyber agent, not an identified affective partner-interaction system governed by this requirement.

review.requirement_proposition: Halt tool registration and operation when unauthorized governance-baseline change is detected, and require explicit re-authorization of the baseline before recovery.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-IN-02 (Halt tool registration and operation when unauthorized governance-baseline change is detected, and require explicit re-authorization of the baseline before recovery.) has a runtime-agent object, but unattended configuration establishes no SDOS undertaking, authorized baseline, integrity-change detection or pre-execution enforcement policy. Disabling approval does not prove applicability of this protocol.

review.reason_for_change: The operator deliberately selected unattended mode. No unauthorised change to a protected governance baseline or recovery from such a change is identified.

review.requirement_proposition: Route governed outbound operations through a pre-execution policy enforcement point that permits, modifies or blocks the operation against current policy and records the decision.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-EN-01 (Route governed outbound operations through a pre-execution policy enforcement point that permits, modifies or blocks the operation against current policy and records the decision.) has a runtime-agent object, but unattended configuration establishes no SDOS undertaking, authorized baseline, integrity-change detection or pre-execution enforcement policy. Disabling approval does not prove applicability of this protocol.

review.reason_for_change: The hostile operator supplied the intrusion objective and selected unattended execution. The actual outbound policy and pre-execution decision records are not available. Victim authorisation is distinct from the operator’s configured execution policy.

review.requirement_proposition: Protocols are put in place to ensure GAI systems are able to be deactivated when necessary.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 GV-1.7-001 (Protocols are put in place to ensure GAI systems are able to be deactivated when necessary.) is a voluntary organizational GAI action. The the July 2026 Hermes intrusion sources do not establish Profile adoption, assigned risk tolerance or the specified deactivation/monitoring/reassessment programme. Configuration, detection and release removal do not establish that named undertaking.

review.reason_for_change: The agent executed unattended actions in a live intrusion. The available account does not show whether deactivation protocols existed or could stop it when needed.

review.requirement_proposition: Provide means to inhibit specified function execution when no authorization to execute is available.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The July 2026 Hermes intrusion involved an operator deliberately selecting unattended/YOLO execution and using the agent after compromise. For IEEE-7009 Annex A.3 / 7009-ASR-011, the missing applicability fact is whether the responsible developer or integrator applied IEEE 7009 to an ASOI exhibiting the required Distinguishing Characteristics and designated the affected operation a specified safety-related or safety-exempt function; ordinary authorisation failure or tool capability does not establish those Annex A.3 conditions. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: The intrusion does not identify a specified safety-function system with the required assurance context. The presence of approval prompts alone does not establish that object.

review.requirement_proposition: Enable assigned overseers, as appropriate and proportionate, to intervene in operation or interrupt the system through a stop mechanism or similar procedure that brings it to a safe state.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 14(4)(e) is later-applying high-risk governance or Article 4a bias-correction permission. the July 2026 Hermes intrusion predates that application/permission and is not special-category processing strictly for bias correction. No general privacy/security duty is substituted for this provision.

review.reason_for_change: The July intrusion in Thailand does not establish a covered Union high-risk AI system or the operative legal oversight conditions.

conclusion_change.previous: This is a real-world deployment of an autonomous agent as offensive cyber tooling. Because a hostile operator deliberately disabled approval prompts and supplied the attack objective, the occurrence does not by itself establish an internal governance failure of Hermes; the material governance issue is the availability and operationalisation of unattended agentic capability in a live government intrusion. The hostile operator selected unattended mode; this is distinct from an applicable approval control failing to activate. Initial access and exfiltration remain unproved, and no named runtime governance undertaking is established.
conclusion_change.new: This is a real-world deployment of an autonomous agent as offensive cyber tooling. Because a hostile operator deliberately disabled approval prompts and supplied the attack objective, the occurrence does not by itself establish an internal governance failure of Hermes; the material governance issue is the availability and operationalisation of unattended agentic capability in a live government intrusion. The hostile operator selected unattended mode; this is distinct from an applicable approval control failing to activate. Initial access and exfiltration remain unproved, and no named runtime governance undertaking is established. The human-approval checkpoint and safe-functioning outcomes are Not aligned for this deployment. The remaining stop, monitoring and outbound-policy assessments are Boundary where their operative records are unavailable.
